# Requirements — Team Chat Application

**Artifact:** Requirements
**Stage:** 2 of 7 (Exercise 2)
**Status:** Final (generated by Claude Opus, critiqued, updated)
**Builds on:** chatapp.assumptions.md

---

## Purpose

This document defines what the chat application must do (functional requirements)
and the qualities it must have (non-functional requirements). Requirements are
derived directly from the assumptions. Each requirement has a unique ID, a
priority (MUST / SHOULD / COULD per MoSCoW), and traces back to the assumption(s)
that motivate it.

---

## 1. Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Traces to |
|----|-------------|----------|-----------|
| FR-01 | A user MUST be able to join the chat by providing a display name. | MUST | A-09, A-28 |
| FR-02 | The system MUST reject an empty or whitespace-only display name. | MUST | A-09 |
| FR-03 | A user MUST be able to send a plain-text message to the shared room. | MUST | A-12, A-13 |
| FR-04 | The system MUST broadcast each sent message to all connected users in near real time. | MUST | A-02, A-16 |
| FR-05 | Each displayed message MUST show the sender's display name and a timestamp. | MUST | A-15 |
| FR-06 | A newly joined user MUST see the recent message history of the room for the current session. | MUST | A-14 |
| FR-07 | The system MUST display a notification when a user joins the room. | SHOULD | A-16 |
| FR-08 | The system MUST display a notification when a user leaves the room. | SHOULD | A-16 |
| FR-09 | The system MUST reject messages that exceed a maximum length (e.g., 2000 characters). | SHOULD | A-13 |
| FR-10 | The system MUST trim and ignore empty/whitespace-only messages. | MUST | A-13 |
| FR-11 | The UI MUST automatically scroll to show the most recent message. | SHOULD | A-10 |
| FR-12 | The system SHOULD show the current count or list of connected users. | COULD | A-16 |
| FR-13 | The system MUST sanitize message content to prevent script injection (XSS). | MUST | A-27 |
| FR-14 | The client MUST automatically attempt to reconnect if the connection drops. | SHOULD | A-25 |

### Out of Scope (MVP)

Authentication beyond a display name, direct/private messages, multiple
channels, threads, file/media sharing, search, presence/typing indicators,
push notifications, message editing/deletion, moderation, and durable
persistence (A-17, A-22, A-28).

---

## 2. Non-Functional Requirements

### 2.1 Performance

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Traces to |
|----|-------------|----------|-----------|
| NFR-01 | A sent message MUST be delivered to other connected clients within ~1 second under normal load. | MUST | A-25 |
| NFR-02 | The application MUST support at least 50 concurrent users on a single instance without degraded delivery. | SHOULD | A-03, A-23 |

### 2.2 Reliability & Availability

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Traces to |
|----|-------------|----------|-----------|
| NFR-03 | The application SHOULD provide best-effort availability with no formal SLA for the MVP. | SHOULD | A-26 |
| NFR-04 | The client MUST recover gracefully from transient disconnects via automatic reconnect. | MUST | A-25, FR-14 |

### 2.3 Security

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Traces to |
|----|-------------|----------|-----------|
| NFR-05 | All traffic MUST be served over HTTPS. | MUST | A-27 |
| NFR-06 | User-supplied content MUST be treated as untrusted and encoded/sanitized before rendering. | MUST | A-27, FR-13 |
| NFR-07 | The architecture MUST NOT preclude adding authentication (e.g., Microsoft Entra ID) later. | SHOULD | A-28 |

### 2.4 Usability & Accessibility

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Traces to |
|----|-------------|----------|-----------|
| NFR-08 | The UI MUST be simple, familiar, and usable without training. | MUST | A-10 |
| NFR-09 | The UI MUST be responsive on desktop and mobile browsers. | SHOULD | A-08 |
| NFR-10 | The UI SHOULD follow basic accessibility practices (keyboard usable, sufficient contrast). | SHOULD | A-30 |

### 2.5 Observability

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Traces to |
|----|-------------|----------|-----------|
| NFR-11 | The application MUST emit structured logs for key events (join, leave, message, errors). | MUST | A-26 |
| NFR-12 | The application MUST be instrumented with OpenTelemetry for traces and metrics. | MUST | A-26 |

### 2.6 Maintainability & Deployment

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Traces to |
|----|-------------|----------|-----------|
| NFR-13 | The application MUST be built with C# and .NET 10. | MUST | A-18 |
| NFR-14 | Real-time delivery MUST use ASP.NET Core SignalR. | MUST | A-19 |
| NFR-15 | The application MUST be deployable to Azure App Service as a single unit. | MUST | A-20, A-21 |
| NFR-16 | The MVP MAY store messages and connection state in memory. | COULD | A-22 |

---

## 3. Acceptance Criteria (Top-Level)

The MVP is accepted when:

1. A user can open the web app, enter a display name, and join the shared room. (FR-01)
2. Two or more users in the room can exchange messages that appear for everyone within ~1 second. (FR-03, FR-04, NFR-01)
3. Each message shows sender and timestamp; join/leave notifications appear. (FR-05, FR-07, FR-08)
4. The app is reachable over HTTPS on Azure App Service. (NFR-05, NFR-15)
5. OpenTelemetry traces/metrics and structured logs are emitted. (NFR-11, NFR-12)

---

## 4. Requirements Traceability Summary

Every functional requirement traces to at least one assumption, and every
top-level acceptance criterion traces to one or more requirements. Downstream
artifacts (functional specifications, test cases, and architecture) reference
these IDs to maintain end-to-end traceability.
